proof_summary: Couple the evolutions from masses \(n\) and \(n+1\) by a single extra grain, which moves one site right exactly when the mass beneath it is odd; the larger system is stable precisely when the smaller one is stable and this grain has reached site \(n\). Hole-freeness, mass conservation, an invariant locating a non-unit cell near the grain, and the classification of the unique nonstable predecessor as \([1^{n-2},2]\) force the grain to be at \(n-1\) or \(n-2\) when the smaller system first stabilizes, after which it moves right once per step and reaches \(n\) exactly one or two steps later.
